Four /30 links: R1-R2 10.0.12.1/.2, R1-R3 10.0.13.1/.2, R2-R4 10.0.24.1/.2, R3-R4 10.0.34.1/.2. R1 Gi0/0 LAN192.168.10.1/24 hosts PC1 .10; R4 Gi0/0 LAN192.168.40.1/24 hosts SRV1 .10. Gateways .1. Interface addressing is prepared without router BGP, static or IGP routes. R2/R3 are deliberately independent transit routers in the same neighboring AS to isolate the default MED comparison, not a complete provider-AS design.

verificationNotes: Four baseline IOS configurations plus distinct MED, AS prepend, local preference and weight command sets are exported and executed. Existing TCP/BGP/CEF/packet engine unchanged. Eight directed sessions require actual received TCP179 OPEN, KEEPALIVE and UPDATE. Both same-prefix external candidates must remain eligible and exactly one selected route must install; static routes, ECMP and always-compare-med overrides fail the intended contract.

Practice starts0/14 and baseline converges to five live goals. Completed reference starts8/14 from saved final configuration with empty runtime and no fabricated traffic achievements. Five stage-specific forward tests plus a real reverse test are needed to reach14. Reference instructions explain reversing policy to revisit stages, then restoring final state and saving all routers.

State fingerprints and per-attempt observation epochs reject old packets from a prior attribute stage, including two stages with the same next hop. Real source send, delivered request, each selected router egress and received frame, and a parent-correlated echo reply prove actual forwarding. Only achievements persist; protocol runtime and observation epochs rebuild on portable reload. Current peer, path, policy, RIB and save checks remain live.

Same-AS MED comparison uses lower50 versus100 with earlier attributes equal; shorter AS path beats the lower MED; localpref200 then overrides the longer AS path; Cisco weight300 overrides that local preference. Inbound local preference and local weight are not advertised to external peers. R3 outbound prepend does not alter its own selected server path.

Tests cover real UPDATE non-delivery, unbound maps, same TCP channel/uptime during soft policy changes, stale-stage packet rejection, packet-proof tampering, unrelated/failed pings, candidate-loss failover and recovery, policy/save drift, IOS reload, portable reopening, bounded imported criteria and every published IOS/Windows verification command.

Scope is the four stated attribute comparisons with origin, route type and other earlier criteria held equal. No claim to exercise the entire Cisco algorithm, locally originated comparisons, origin-code preference, eBGP/iBGP, IGP next-hop cost, ECMP or later tie breakers. No new live CML capture or platform-wide parity claim.
Existing layout, simulation engine and terminal styling preserved; current-host/path/query permalink and independent catalog sections retained. Historical validation reports remain unchanged.
